subject: Agriculture
title: Invasive Species
description: A micro-lesson that makes Invasive Species usable.

hook.text: The fall armyworm spread from the Americas to Africa in 2016 and to Asia by 2018. It now threatens all tropics.

buildup.text: Global trade and climate change accelerate pest invasions. Ships, planes, and warming open new territories.

discovery.text: Fall armyworm can eat 80 different crop species and flies 100 km per night. Nothing stops its spread.

twist.text: Native parasitoids and predators can't control it—they've never encountered it. Natural defenses are absent.

climax.text: Invasive pests cost global agriculture $70 billion per year and rising as trade and temperatures increase.

punchline.text: Pests travel the same trade routes as goods. Borders don't stop biology.

quiz.question: How far can fall armyworm travel in a single night?

details.summary: Invasive agricultural pests are species introduced to regions where they have no natural predators, allowing them to cause devastating crop damage. This topic covers how invasive species spread through global trade, their economic impact, and efforts to prevent and manage invasions.
details.whyItMatters: Global trade and climate change are accelerating the spread of invasive pests into new regions. The fall armyworm spread across all of sub-Saharan Africa in just two years, demonstrating how quickly invasive pests can threaten food security.
takeaways: Invasive pests cost global agriculture over $70 billion annually in crop losses
Global trade, travel, and climate change are accelerating pest invasions worldwide
Early detection and rapid response are the most cost-effective management strategies

faq.question: How do invasive pest species spread to new agricultural regions?
faq.answer: Invasive pests spread through contaminated plant material in trade shipments, in soil attached to imports, as stowaways on ships and aircraft, and by natural flight or wind dispersal once established nearby. Climate change also makes previously inhospitable regions suitable for new pests.

faq.question: What is the most recent major invasive crop pest?
faq.answer: The fall armyworm, native to the Americas, was detected in Africa in 2016 and spread across the entire continent and into Asia within two years. It attacks over 80 crop species, primarily maize, and now threatens food security for hundreds of millions of people.
